root_cause.text: The write-side critical section in `fprop_new_period()` was not protected against hardirqs, allowing a hardirq to attempt a read seqlock on the same sequence counter while the write lock was held, causing a deadlock.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces `preempt_disable_nested()` with `local_irq_save()` / `local_irq_restore()` around the `write_seqcount_begin/end` calls. The CVE description details the exact race: in softirq context, `fprop_new_period()` holds the write seqlock, then a hardirq triggers a read on the same sequence counter, which spins indefinitely because the sequence count is odd. The commit message states the fix is to make the write section irqsafe.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix seqlock write-side synchronization by disabling interrupts to protect against concurrent access in interrupt context.
intent_record.what: Replaced preempt_disable_nested() with local_irq_save(flags) in fprop_new_period(), adding unsigned long flags variable.
intent_record.how: The change disables local interrupts instead of just preemption during the seqlock write critical section, preventing interrupt handlers from reading the sequence counter while it is being updated.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix incorrect pairing of synchronization primitives by replacing preempt_enable_nested() with local_irq_restore(flags) to properly restore IRQ state.
intent_record.how: Previously, after the write sequence count unlock, the code attempted to re-enable preemption via `preempt_enable_nested()`. Now it restores the interrupt flags saved earlier via `local_irq_save(flags)`, correcting the synchronization to properly re-enable interrupts instead of only preemption.
